solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He charges coppers in a tree

indicators.note: the coppers are placed in the tree, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the acer is a maple tree
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so two coppers are CUs

explanation.surface: Someone up a tree is levelling charges at the police below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police officers but means the metal's chemical symbol, Cu, made plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who brings charges against another is an accuser, the prosecuting party in a complaint.

clue.text: Slander from rude speakers without a hint of kindness

indicators.note: rude here means rough or crude, so the letters are knocked into a new order
a hint of picks just the opening letter of kindness

explanation.surface: Abuse comes from loudspeakers that lack any kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes K (the first letter of kindness) from SPEAKERS; 'rude' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast aspersions on someone, attacking their reputation.

clue.text: After work's carried out telescope adjusts to sky-blue

indicators.note: carried out means removed, so the work is taken away from the telescope
adjusts suggests changing the arrangement, so the remaining letters are reordered

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Once a job is finished, a telescope is pointed at the blue sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried out' removes OP from TELESCOPE, leaving TELESCE, which 'adjusts' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeste is a sky-blue colour, from the Latin for heavenly.

clue.text: Sportsman hit high in the air

definitions.meaning: a person who races down snowy slopes on skis
in cricket a ball struck very high is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a skier (sometimes skyer) is a ball hit steeply upward, often to be caught.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is someone on skis; the other is a cricket term for a ball struck steeply skyward.

clue.text: With radar around it's nothing to refocus on astronomical object

indicators.note: refocus means adjust again, so the letters are shifted about

parts.note: it's gives its letters without the apostrophe
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Radar is turned around and retuned to look at a body in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refocus' rearranges RADAR, ITS and O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: A radio star is a celestial source emitting strong radio waves, an object studied by astronomers.

clue.text: Extraordinary score by American plutocrat?

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so the letters of score are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American tycoon has notched up a remarkable tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' is the anagram signal; the question mark marks the definition as an example (the Lydian king) rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Croesus, the fabulously rich king of Lydia, is the byword for an extremely wealthy person.

clue.text: Richard's endlessly working being in charge of meetings

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the remaining letters are set in motion and rearranged
endlessly drops the outer letters of the name, keeping its inside

explanation.surface: Richard is forever busy running meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves ICHAR from RICHARD, which 'working' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The chair is the person presiding over a meeting, running its business.

clue.text: Excessive outlay proves awkward to terminate

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsily arranged, so the letters of proves are jumbled

parts.note: to end is to terminate

explanation.surface: Cutting spending that is too high turns out to be tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' turns PROVES into OVERSP.
explanation.definitionFit: An overspend is spending more than budgeted, an excessive outlay of money.

clue.text: St Paul wielded a cooking implement

indicators.note: wielded suggests something swung about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: The apostle Paul brandished a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed kitchen tool for lifting or spreading food.

clue.text: Symbol of authority and respect possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints at another possible arrangement of the word respect

explanation.surface: A token of power commands respect.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental staff held by a monarch is an emblem of sovereign power.

clue.text: Friend with stricken side is paralysed

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: stricken suggests something damaged and knocked out of shape, so the word side is rearranged

explanation.surface: A companion whose side has been struck down cannot move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stricken' is the anagram signal, though it reads as part of the medical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Palsied describes someone affected by palsy, a condition causing paralysis or tremor.

clue.text: Positively declare generation's mean

parts.note: to aver is to state something firmly
an age can be a generation or period

explanation.surface: Someone firmly states what a whole generation intends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like a verb or 'unkind'; it is the noun meaning arithmetic midpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its arithmetic midpoint, the usual sense of the statistical term.

clue.text: Mostly keep Spanish river flowing back into tank

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to keep something back is to reserve it

indicators.note: flowing back tells us the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: rio is the Spanish word for river

explanation.surface: A river runs back into a holding tank to be kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims RESERVE to RESERV; 'flowing back' turns RIO into OIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large storage tank or lake holding a water supply.

clue.text: Deliberately avoid station's second sidetrack

parts.note: to shun is to avoid on purpose

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of station

explanation.surface: A railway train deliberately bypasses the station to wait in a siding.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway surface hides the verb sense: to shunt is to divert.
explanation.definitionFit: To shunt is to move a train onto a siding, and so to divert or push aside, like sidetracking.

clue.text: Colleges that limit discharge

indicators.note: the two words limit or bound the answer, which is concealed within them

explanation.surface: Colleges impose a cap on how many students they release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limit' signals the letters bounded by 'Colleges that'.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge or excrete from the body, the opposite of ingesting.

clue.text: Invitation to sit?

parts.note: the polite phrase used when offering someone a chair; the question mark nods at how plain it is

explanation.definitionFit: Asking a visitor to be seated is the usual courteous offer of a chair.

clue.text: Spoons etc, to bale water spilt

indicators.note: spilt water is scattered about, so the letters of bale and water are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cutlery is used to scoop up some spilt water.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoons, forks and plates are all items of tableware, the utensils used at a meal.

clue.text: He directs a young star in dance

parts.note: a boss is the one who gives directions
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens, taken loosely as a new one

explanation.surface: A director features a rising starlet in a dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'young star' plays on nova, Latin for new.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to samba.

clue.text: Obi-man uses these dark skills

parts.note: an obi-man practises obeah, Caribbean sorcery, so his skills are magic of the sinister kind

explanation.surface: A sorcerer employs sinister talents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obi-man' looks like a Star Wars nod; an obi (obeah) man is a Caribbean sorcerer.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic and witchcraft are called the dark arts, sinister skills of sorcery.

clue.text: It should help you travel to resort in Dutch vessel

indicators.note: the resort is put inside the vessel

parts.note: a buss is a two-masted Dutch herring boat
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Taking a Dutch boat to a holiday resort helps you get around.
explanation.walkthrough: A buss is an old Dutch fishing boat. A bus pass is a ticket for free or cheap bus travel, common for UK pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel card for buses lets the holder ride, so it helps them get about.

clue.text: Pillow torn inside in the style of Ireland's darling

indicators.note: the shortened pillow goes inside the phrase meaning in the style of

parts.note: a la is French for in the style of

indicators.note: torn means ripped off, so the word for pillow loses its end

parts.note: a cushion is a soft pillow

explanation.surface: An Irish sweetheart's pillow gets ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' cuts the pillow word short, dropping its last three letters, and 'inside' puts what remains within the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Acushla is an Irish term of endearment meaning sweetheart or dear one.

clue.text: Stone thrown for famous seafarer

definitions.meaning: in the game ducks and ... a flat pebble is skimmed across water, and such a throw is called a ...
Sir Francis ... was the Elizabethan navigator who sailed round the world

explanation.walkthrough: Ducks and drakes is a game of skimming flat stones across water.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake circumnavigated the globe; a skimmed pebble in ducks and drakes is also named this way.

clue.text: Poison, one finds it in an ice cream cornet

parts.note: an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: it is placed inside the cornet

parts.note: a cone is an ice cream cornet

explanation.surface: Someone finds poison in their ice cream cornet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a highly toxic plant poison.

clue.text: Among the world's severest challenges

indicators.note: among means amid, so the answer lies inside the word severest

explanation.surface: This is one of the toughest tests on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The mountain sits inside 'severest', and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is one of the hardest climbing feats on the planet.

clue.text: One puts back Buddhist shrine

indicators.note: back says the word puts is read the other way

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Someone returns an object to a Buddhist shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PUTS into STUP; A for 'One' goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupa is a dome-shaped Buddhist monument housing relics, a type of shrine.

clue.text: French chalk polluted teaspoons

indicators.note: polluted means corrupted or spoiled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Chalk from France has contaminated some teaspoons.
explanation.definitionFit: French chalk is a form of talc, and soapstone is a soft talc-rich rock.

clue.text: Recording that's pronounced shabby

indicators.note: pronounced tells us the abbreviation is said out loud

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording

explanation.surface: A recording is described as scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters C D, spoken, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means run-down and disreputable, like a shabby back-street bar.

clue.text: Allows to climb a stone slab

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upward, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: lets means allows

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to clamber up a slab of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns LETS into STEL in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright carved slab used as a monument or gravestone.

clue.text: One allowed in heat running?

indicators.note: the allowed word is placed inside the scrambled heat
running signals the letters of heat are moved about

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: Is this someone permitted to compete in a race heat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' turns HEAT into ATHE; the whole clue also describes a runner in a heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor admitted to a running heat is a sportsman or sportswoman on the track.

clue.text: A prison sentence is past

parts.note: the article a stands for the number one
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A jail term is over and done with.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time means former, describing something now in the past.

clue.text: Will's tinker closes trade quickly

indicators.note: closes means encloses, so the tinker's name surrounds the trade

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew; Will is Shakespeare
a mart is a market, a place of trade

explanation.surface: A tinker shuts up shop in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is William Shakespeare, whose Taming of the Shrew opens with the tinker Christopher Sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartly can mean briskly or promptly, as in stepping smartly forward.

clue.text: A waster after reform becomes most informed

indicators.note: after being reformed the waster is remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A layabout who mends their ways ends up best educated.
explanation.definitionFit: Aware means knowing or informed, and the superlative is the most informed.
